Hi Lisa / Helix procurement team,

Thanks again for the demonstration yesterday — appreciate the time. As promised, attaching our proposed redlines to the MSA + Order Form focused on the SLA and maintenance language so legal and procurement can review. High-level summary below: 

- Uptime measurement: propose regional availability (per-region 99.95% monthly) with per-API endpoint measurement window of 5 minutes.
- Service credits: tiered credits (see table on p.2 of the PDF) with cap at 50% of monthly fees for a single month.
- Response tiers: P1 (1 hour initial ack), P2 (4 hours), P3 (24 hours) — with business-hour vs. 24x7 distinctions called out.
- Maintenance windows: regular maintenance limited to two 4-hour windows per month per region; 72-hour advance notice for planned maintenance; emergency maintenance carveouts clearly defined.

Next steps: please review the PDF redline and call out any absolute no-go items. If acceptable, we can propose a short call next week to walk through the changes and lock a final Order Form for signature.

Thanks, Jonas. Quick clarifying questions from our side before we loop in our legal: 

1) Uptime measurement: when you say "per-region" — is that per cloud region that hosts our traffic, or per-availability-zone? In our case we run a cross-region failover and want to avoid double-crediting.
2) Maintenance blackout: can you confirm if any customer-visible cutover during a major model patch would be considered "planned" (with 72-hour notice) or "emergency" (no notice)? For large model upgrades this matters for our support windows.
3) Credits cap: Helix procurement tends to push for a cap lower than 50% for single-month incidents — can you share the rationale for your upper bound?

We attached our internal procurement playbook excerpt for context. Happy to set a legal-to-legal review later this week.

—Lisa

Lisa — thanks for the fast feedback. Looping in Marissa (legal) to provide formal language and rationale; quick responses inline below so procurement has context before legal weighs in: 

1) Per-region meaning: per-cloud-region (e.g., us-west-2). We use per-region because customers with multi-region failover would not be double-credited; credits are computed per-region and only triggered if that region's availability falls below the threshold. We can add an explicit clause to exclude failover artifacts from the calculation.

2) Planned vs emergency: major model upgrades that can be scheduled with no customer impact would be planned (72-hour notice). Major model upgrades that require immediate rollout due to security or safety fixes would be emergency and fall into the emergency maintenance carveout. We can add a definition for "customer-impacting" vs. "non-customer-impacting" maintenance.

3) Credits cap rationale: 50% cap is to preserve incentives on both sides and avoid outsized refunds for rare catastrophic events; open to negotiation — Marissa, do you want to propose alternative cap language?

I've pasted the key bullets from the redline into the attached short summary for legal. Would you be available for a 30-minute legal-to-legal call on Friday?

Thanks,

Hi Lisa / Helix procurement team — Marissa from Redwood Legal. I reviewed Jonas' redlines and have prepared firm language we believe balances Helix's availability requirements with operational realities. Key legal redlines are below (attached as tracked changes in the Order Form doc):

- Availability measurement: define "region" as the cloud region where the tenant's primary traffic is routed; exclude brief failover occurrences (less than 5 minutes) from downtime calculations. Also include a clause that scheduled failovers performed by customer will not be counted as Redwood downtime.

- Service credits matrix (proposed):
  * < 99.9% monthly — 10% credit of monthly invoice for affected region
  * 99.5% - 99.9% — 25% credit
  * < 99.5% — 50% credit (cap per-month 50%)
  Credits apply only to usage fees (not one-time fees). Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for availability failures.

- Response SLA: P1 (Severity 1) initial acknowledgement within 1 hour, on-call engineer engaged within 2 hours; P2 initial acknowledgement within 4 hours; P3 within 24 hours. For paid enterprise support (24x7) exceptions can be codified in the Order Form.

- Maintenance windows: Redwood will provide at least 72 hours' notice for planned maintenance. Routine maintenance will be scheduled during the single weekly 4-hour maintenance window selected by the customer. The Order Form will allow customers to select one standard maintenance window per region; additional windows may be scheduled by mutual agreement.

- Emergency maintenance carveout: defined as actions required to prevent imminent customer-impacting security, privacy, or safety incidents. Redwood will notify customers as soon as practicable and provide a post-event summary. Emergency maintenance will not be eligible for service credits unless Redwood is at fault for the outage.

- Aggregation and measurement: metrics are computed using the Redwood telemetry ingestion pipeline; customers will receive monthly measurement reports and may dispute measurement within 30 days with reasonable evidence.

If Helix can confirm the following items, we can prepare a counter-signed Order Form:
1) Which region(s) Helix considers "primary" for this integration (list cloud regions).
2) Whether Helix requires a lower cap on credits for business reasons (we can propose a middle ground at 40%).
3) Which maintenance window (day/time) Helix prefers for routine maintenance.

Attachments: OrderForm_SLA_marked.docx [tracked changes]
